body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「換咗 model 後，邊一組 evidence 先足以決定 release 或 rollback？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「用 LLM-as-a-judge 算平均分。」

平均分可以幫你看趨勢，但它不會替你定義『哪個錯不能接受』，也不會告訴你哪一次改動造成 regression。Release decision 要把 candidate、known baseline、固定 case、owner 和可逆動作扣在一起；否則 dashboard 變紅時，你只知道有人不滿，卻不知道怎樣安全回到上一個狀態。

## 先把 release 拆成三個不同的判斷

第一個是 evaluation 判斷：candidate 在固定 synthetic cases 上有沒有保持必要 behaviour，例如不支持的 citation、該交接卻亂答、schema 不合或不該叫 tool 的 case 都要失敗。第二個是 reviewer 判斷：抽樣或指定高風險 cases 是否真的可用，grader 是否漏掉重要 caveat。第三個才是 rollout 判斷：由誰批准、哪一小組可見、保存哪個 baseline、甚麼 signal 會觸發回退。把三者混成『score 過關就 deploy』，就失去每個 gate 的用途。

## 每次變更都要有一張收據

候選輸出不能只記 model name。記錄 prompt／system instruction、model ID 和 settings、retrieval or index snapshot、tool policy、parser、evaluation rubric、fixture version 和 deployment route。每次 run 產生一份 change receipt，連回 baseline 對照、case-level result、latency 和 cost proxy。若一個 case 退步，先知道它是哪一種 failure，才決定修 prompt、資料、模型、route 或根本不應推出。

## Rollback 是一個可演練的動作

在本地 demo 裡，也要寫清楚安全 baseline 是甚麼：例如保留原來只草擬、不自動提交的 route，或只顯示搜尋結果而不生成 policy conclusion。預先定 rollback trigger，如 high-severity citation failure、tool call 超出 scope、指定 critical case fail、p99 超出限制或 reviewer 拒絕率升高；再定誰可以啟動、要保留哪段 trace、以及 user 會看到甚麼。Rollback 不是『改回舊版』四個字，而是可執行的 route switch 加一份可追查紀錄。

## 面試時怎樣避免過度承諾

可以答：『我會把 candidate 和 baseline 在固定 cases 上做 case-level 比較，自動 score 只是一條訊號。高風險 case 由 reviewer 校準；推出前先留安全 baseline 和明確 trigger，任何一個不可接受 failure 都回到 baseline。』這不聲稱本地 fixture 證明 production ready，卻交代了下一步如何累積足夠 evidence。

## reviewer 可以核對甚麼

- **工程：** versioned fixtures、baseline/candidate diff、grader 校準樣本、trace receipt、rollback route test。
- **交付：** release owner、reviewer、受影響 user 範圍、公告或 handoff 文字，以及由誰確認回退後系統仍可用。
- **風險：** 清楚寫下不接受的 failure，並保留一個 candidate 得分較好但仍被擋下的案例。

## 延伸閱讀

[Eval score 要經過真人 calibration](/zh-HK/interview-lab/an-eval-score-needs-human-calibration)、[Rollout 要有安全 baseline](/zh-HK/interview-lab/a-rollout-needs-a-safe-baseline) 和 [Prompt versioning 唔等於 audit trail](/zh-HK/interview-lab/prompt-versioning-is-not-an-audit-trail)。

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。release、rollback、review 和 metrics 均為 synthetic 本地教學設計；它不證明任何產品已部署、已獲批准或已在 production 運作。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “After changing the model, which evidence is enough to choose release or rollback?”
>
> Half-right answer: “I would calculate an average LLM-as-a-judge score.”

An average can reveal a trend. It cannot define which error is unacceptable, nor identify which change created a regression. A release decision needs to join a candidate, known baseline, fixed cases, owner and reversible action; otherwise a red dashboard only tells you that someone is unhappy, not how to return safely to a prior state.

## Separate release into three decisions

First is the evaluation decision: does a candidate preserve necessary behaviour on fixed synthetic cases? Unsupported citations, unsupported answers where handoff is required, invalid schema, and impermissible tool calls must all be failures. Second is the reviewer decision: are sampled or nominated high-risk cases truly usable, and does the grader miss an important caveat? Third is the rollout decision: who approves, which small audience can see it, what baseline remains, and which signal triggers a return. Combining all three as ‘the score passed, deploy’ removes the purpose of each gate.

## Give every change a receipt

A candidate result needs more than a model name. Record the prompt/system instruction, model ID and settings, retrieval or index snapshot, tool policy, parser, evaluation rubric, fixture version and deployment route. Each run produces a change receipt that links back to its baseline comparison, case-level result, latency and cost proxy. If a case regresses, first identify its failure type; then decide whether to change a prompt, data, model, route, or decline the release altogether.

## Rollback is an action you can rehearse

Even in a local demo, name the safe baseline: perhaps the original draft-only route with no submission, or search results without a generated policy conclusion. Predefine triggers such as a high-severity citation failure, a tool call outside scope, a failed critical case, p99 above a limit, or a higher reviewer rejection rate. Then name who can trigger the return, which trace survives, and what the user sees. Rollback is not four words meaning ‘switch back’; it is an executable route switch plus an inspectable record.

## Avoiding an overclaim in an interview

You can answer: ‘I compare candidate and baseline case by case on fixed fixtures; the automated score is one signal. A reviewer calibrates high-risk cases. Before any rollout I retain a safe baseline and clear triggers, and one unacceptable failure returns the route to baseline.’ That does not pretend local fixtures prove production readiness, but it explains how the next evidence is accumulated.

## What a reviewer can check

- **Engineering:** versioned fixtures, baseline/candidate diffs, grader-calibration samples, trace receipts and a rollback-route test.
- **Delivery:** release owner, reviewer, affected-user scope, notice or handoff copy, and who confirms the system remains usable after returning.
- **Risk:** an explicit list of unacceptable failures and a case where the higher-scoring candidate was still blocked.

## Further reading

[An evaluation score needs human calibration](/en/interview-lab/an-eval-score-needs-human-calibration), [A rollout needs a safe baseline](/en/interview-lab/a-rollout-needs-a-safe-baseline), and [Prompt versioning is not an audit trail](/en/interview-lab/prompt-versioning-is-not-an-audit-trail).

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. Release, rollback, review and metrics are synthetic local teaching design; they do not prove that any product is deployed, approved or operating in production.
